subject: Hygiene Development
content: Community hygiene means keeping shared spaces clean: markets, schools, parks, water sources, public toilets. Everyone's responsibility. Actions: dispose trash properly, don't litter, keep drains clear, report sanitation issues, participate in community clean-ups, protect water sources from contamination. In Nigeria, community hygiene prevents diseases like cholera (from contaminated water) and malaria (from stagnant water). Many communities have monthly sanitation days. Youth environmental clubs lead hygiene campaigns. Good community hygiene shows respect for neighbors and future generations.
summary: Community hygiene = keeping shared spaces clean. Dispose trash, clear drains, participate in clean-ups, protect water. Prevents cholera, malaria.

quiz_questions.question: What disease spreads from contaminated water?
quiz_questions.explanation: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and poor sanitation.

subject: Hygiene Development
content: Mental hygiene means taking care of your emotional and psychological health. Practices: talk about feelings with trusted people, manage stress (deep breathing, exercise, sleep), set boundaries (say no when needed), practice gratitude, limit screen time, spend time in nature, pursue hobbies, ask for help when struggling. Mental hygiene prevents anxiety, depression, burnout. Nigerian proverb: 'Health is not valued until sickness comes.' Mental health equals physical health. Reduce stigma by speaking openly. Schools increasingly have counselors. You are not alone.
summary: Mental hygiene = emotional/psychological health. Talk about feelings, manage stress, set boundaries, practice gratitude, get help. Reduce stigma.

quiz_questions.question: What is mental hygiene?
quiz_questions.explanation: Mental hygiene prevents anxiety, depression, burnout.

subject: Hygiene Development
content: Environmental health studies how surroundings affect human health. Hazards: air pollution (generator fumes, bush burning), water pollution (industrial waste, sewage), soil contamination (chemicals, improper waste), noise pollution, climate change (flooding, heat waves). Protection: use clean cookstoves, don't burn trash, boil water, plant trees, recycle, support clean energy. Nigerian environmental agencies: NESREA (National Environmental Standards). Individual actions matter. Healthy environment = healthy people. Future careers: environmental health officer, pollution control specialist.
summary: Environmental health = how surroundings affect health. Hazards: air, water, noise pollution, climate change. Protection: clean cookstoves, boil water, plant trees.

quiz_questions.question: What agency enforces environmental standards in Nigeria?
quiz_questions.explanation: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency.

subject: Communication
content: Digital communication uses electronic tools: email, instant messaging, video calls, social media. Best practices: think before sending (can't unsend), use clear subject lines, be concise, respect privacy (don't share others' messages), avoid all caps (shouting), use proper grammar/spelling, respond in reasonable time, don't engage with trolls, remember digital footprint (everything online is permanent). Nigerian youth use WhatsApp, Instagram, Twitter, Zoom. Cyberbullying is harmful - report it. Balance online and offline relationships. Digital communication skills matter for school, work, and life.
summary: Digital communication: email, messaging, video, social media. Think before sending, respect privacy, avoid all caps, remember permanent record.

quiz_questions.question: What is a digital footprint?
quiz_questions.explanation: Everything you post leaves traces others can see.

subject: Communication
content: Public relations (PR) manages communication between organizations and public. Goal: build positive reputation. PR tools: press releases (official announcements), media interviews, social media posts, events, crisis communication (handling problems). Nigerian PR practitioners work for companies, government, NGOs, celebrities. PR skills: writing, speaking, relationship building, problem-solving, ethics. Students practice PR in school: promoting events, writing newsletters, managing class reputation. Example: when a product fails, PR explains what happened and steps to fix. Honesty is essential - lying destroys trust.
summary: PR manages communication between organizations and public. Tools: press releases, media, social media, events, crisis communication. Builds reputation.

quiz_questions.question: What is press release?
quiz_questions.explanation: Press releases inform journalists about news.

subject: Leadership
content: Transformational leadership inspires people to achieve extraordinary outcomes. Four components: idealized influence (leading by example, ethics), inspirational motivation (articulating compelling vision), intellectual stimulation (encouraging innovation, creativity), individualized consideration (coaching, mentoring). Transformational leaders: Martin Luther King Jr., Nelson Mandela, Nigerian leaders like Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. Unlike transactional leadership (rewards/punishments), transformational changes organizations. You can practice: share vision, praise creativity, mentor younger students, lead by example. Transformational leadership creates positive change.
summary: Transformational leadership inspires extraordinary outcomes. Four components: idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, individualized consideration.

quiz_questions.question: What is idealized influence?
quiz_questions.explanation: Leaders model desired behaviors and values.

subject: Leadership
content: Servant leadership prioritizes serving others first, then leading. Ten principles: listening, empathy, healing (helping resolve conflicts), awareness, persuasion (not coercion), conceptualization (big picture thinking), foresight, stewardship (responsibility for organization), commitment to growth, building community. Nigerian traditional leaders (Obas, Emirs, Igwes) often embody servant leadership - they serve their communities. Modern examples: teachers who support students, coaches who develop players. Servant leaders ask: 'How can I help you succeed?' Leadership is not about power - it's about service.
summary: Servant leadership serves others first. Ten principles: listening, empathy, healing, awareness, persuasion, foresight, stewardship, growth, community.

quiz_questions.question: What question do servant leaders ask?
options: How can I help you succeed?
quiz_questions.correct_answer: How can I help you succeed?
quiz_questions.explanation: Servant leaders prioritize others' success over their own.

subject: Teamwork
content: Virtual teams work together online from different locations. Tools: Zoom, Slack, Google Docs, Trello, WhatsApp. Challenges: time zones, technology issues, less personal connection, miscommunication. Success strategies: clear communication (over-communicate), use video (builds trust), document decisions, set meeting times, respect time zones, use shared calendars, celebrate wins virtually. Nigerian students collaborate online for group projects using Google Docs and WhatsApp. Virtual teamwork skills are essential for future jobs. Practice: agree on communication tools, assign roles, meet regularly, update each other.
summary: Virtual teams work online from different locations. Tools: Zoom, Slack, Google Docs. Challenges: time zones, tech issues. Strategies: clear communication, video, documentation.

quiz_questions.question: What tool is best for real-time document collaboration?
quiz_questions.explanation: Multiple people can edit same document simultaneously.

subject: Teamwork
content: Cross-functional teams include members from different departments or skills working toward common goal. Example: launching new product needs marketing, design, engineering, finance. Benefits: diverse perspectives, faster problem-solving, innovation. Challenges: different priorities, communication barriers, turf wars. Success factors: clear shared goal, mutual respect, good facilitation, regular communication. Nigerian businesses use cross-functional teams for projects. In school, science projects need research, writing, art, presentation skills - each student contributes different strengths. Cross-functional experience valuable for future careers.
summary: Cross-functional teams have members from different skills/departments. Benefits: diverse perspectives, innovation. Challenges: different priorities. Success: clear goal, respect.

quiz_questions.question: What is cross-functional team?
quiz_questions.explanation: Members bring diverse expertise to solve complex problems.

subject: Creativity
content: Creative strategy plans how to develop innovative solutions. Steps: understand the challenge, research (gather inspiration), brainstorm many ideas (quantity over quality), select promising ideas, develop concept, test, refine. Tools: mind mapping (visual connections), SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse), reverse thinking (opposite approach), random word association. Nigerian entrepreneurs use creative strategy to solve local problems: mobile payment (Paga, Flutterwave), solar solutions, waste recycling, agro-tech. Document your process. Creative strategy applies to business, art, science, daily life.
summary: Creative strategy plans innovative solutions. Steps: understand, research, brainstorm, select, develop, test, refine. Tools: mind maps, SCAMPER, reverse thinking.

subject: Creativity
content: Innovation management is systematically developing and implementing new ideas. Stages: idea generation (soliciting internal/external ideas), screening (select promising ideas), concept development (detailed plan), prototyping (build simple version), testing (get feedback), commercialization (launch). Intrapreneurship = employees acting like entrepreneurs within organizations. Nigerian companies invest in R&D (research & development). Innovation culture encourages: psychological safety (no punishment for failed experiments), time for creative work, rewards for good ideas, cross-functional collaboration. Managing innovation balances creativity with practical constraints.
summary: Innovation management develops new ideas systematically. Stages: idea generation, screening, concept development, prototyping, testing, launch. Innovation culture: safety, time, rewards.
